His earliest published writings appeared in 1916 in Morgunblaðið and in the children's periodical Æskan.[6] The same year, two letters-to-the-editor Halldór wrote also appeared in the North American-Icelandic children's newspapers Sólskin, which was published in Winnipeg, Manitoba.[7] Laxness then attended and in 1918 graduated from the Reykjavík Lyceum.[8] By the time his first novel, Barn náttúrunnar (Child of Nature, 1919), was published he had already begun his travels on the European continent.[9].
